intros.text: Amos was a shepherd who spoke the Lord's message around 760 b.c. Though Amos was born in the southern kingdom of Judah, the Lord tells him to travel to Bethel and preach in Israel, the northern kingdom, and to announce that the nations of Syria, Philistia, Phoenicia, Edom, Ammon, Moab, and Judah will be punished. However, the longest message of punishment Amos delivers is for Israel itself because the wealthy people there were mistreating those who were poor and helpless. The message of judgment against Israel is in the form of five visions: locusts that will destroy all the food; fire that will burn everything on earth; a measuring line that shows the Israelites they do not meet God's standards of faithfulness; a basket of ripe fruit that shows that the people are ready for destruction; and the collapse of the Bethel temple and death of the people worshiping there. The Lord promises to scatter the people of Israel among other nations. But the final message in Amos is one of hope; it promises that the Lord will rebuild the kingdom and its people will once again prosper. Outline Messages of Judgment against Israel and Its Neighbors (1.1—6.14) Visions of Israel's Punishment and Renewal (7.1—9.15)

verses.text: I am Amos. And I raised sheep near the town of Tekoa when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel. Two years before the earthquake, the LORD gave me several messages about Israel,

footnotes.text: Tekoa: In the hill country of Judah about eight kilometers south of Bethlehem.
Uzziah … Jeroboam: Uzziah was king of Judah 781–740 b.c., and Jeroboam II was king of Israel 783–743 b.c.
Jehoash: The Hebrew text has “Joash,” another spelling of the name.
Two years … earthquake: Possibly the earthquake of 760 b.c., which seems to have been especially violent.
messages: Or “visions.”

verses.text: and I said: When the LORD roars from Jerusalem, pasturelands and Mount Carmel dry up and turn brown.
The LORD said: I will punish Syria for countless crimes, and I won't change my mind. They dragged logs with spikes over the people of Gilead.

footnotes.text: Syria: The Hebrew text has “Damascus,” the leading city of Syria.
logs with spikes: These were dragged over grain to thresh it.

verses.text: Now I will burn down the palaces and fortresses of King Hazael and of King Benhadad.

footnotes.text: Hazael … Benhadad: Two Syrian kings.

verses.text: I will break through the gates of Damascus. I will destroy the people of Wicked Valley and the ruler of Beth-Eden. Then the Syrians will be dragged as prisoners to Kir. I, the LORD, have spoken!

footnotes.text: people: Or “king.”
Wicked Valley: The Hebrew text has “Aven Valley,” probably the fertile valley between the Lebanon and the Anti-Lebanon mountains.
I will … Beth-Eden: Or “I will destroy the people of Wicked Valley and the king who rules from Beth-Eden.” Beth-Eden was a city-state on the banks of the Euphrates River.

Kir: The exact location of this country is not known; in 9.7 Amos refers to Kir as the original home of the Syrians, and so the verse probably means that the Syrians will lose everything they have gained as a people.

verses.text: The LORD said: I will punish Philistia for countless crimes, and I won't change my mind. They dragged off my people from town after town to sell them as slaves to the Edomites.

footnotes.text: Philistia: The Hebrew text has “Gaza,” one of the main Philistine cities.
my people: The people of Israel.

verses.text: That's why I will burn down the walls and fortresses of the city of Gaza.
I will destroy the king of Ashdod and the ruler of Ashkelon. I will strike down Ekron, and that will be the end of the Philistines. I, the LORD, have spoken!

footnotes.text: king: Or “people.”
Ashdod … Ashkelon … Ekron: Philistine cities.

verses.text: The LORD said: I will punish Phoenicia for countless crimes, and I won't change my mind. They broke their treaty and dragged off my people from town after town to sell them as slaves to the Edomites.

footnotes.text: Phoenicia: The Hebrew text has “Tyre,” which was one of the two Phoenician cities; the other was Sidon, which is not mentioned by Amos.
my people: See the note at 1.6.

verses.text: That's why I will send flames to burn down the city of Tyre along with its fortresses.
The LORD said: I will punish Edom for countless crimes, and I won't change my mind. They killed their own relatives and were so terribly furious that they showed no mercy.

footnotes.text: their own relatives: The Edomites were descendants of Esau, the brother of Jacob, the ancestor of the Israelites.

verses.text: Now I will send fire to wipe out the fortresses of Teman and Bozrah.

footnotes.text: Teman and Bozrah: These stand for all of Edom; Teman may have been a city or a district. Bozrah, the chief city of northern Edom, was 48 kilometers southeast of the Dead Sea.

verses.text: The LORD said: I will punish Ammon for countless crimes, and I won't change my mind. In Gilead they ripped open pregnant women, just to take the land.
Now I will send fire to destroy the walls and fortresses of Rabbah. Enemies will shout and attack like a whirlwind.

footnotes.text: Rabbah: The capital city of Ammon.

verses.text: Ammon's king and leaders will be dragged away. I, the LORD, have spoken!
